claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy is single-phase BCC.
The initial TiVNbTa alloy has a dendritic microstructure.
Standard processing produces TiVNbTa containing approximately 1–3 at% oxygen and nitrogen impurities.
Ultra-high-purity processing or degassing/gettering can drastically reduce oxygen and nitrogen during TiVNbTa synthesis.
Reducing oxygen and nitrogen will inhibit impurity-promoted phase segregation during high-temperature exposure.
Trace oxygen and nitrogen promote phase segregation in TiVNbTa during thermal aging.
Thermal-aging-induced segregation depletes strengthening interstitial solutes from the TiVNbTa matrix.
Depletion of interstitial solutes from the matrix causes progressive softening during aging.
Oxygen and nitrogen initially contribute to solid-solution strengthening in TiVNbTa.
Purifying TiVNbTa will maintain a homogeneous single-phase BCC structure without deleterious segregated phases or precipitates.
Minimizing interstitials will preserve the dislocation-pinning benefits of a uniform interstitial distribution.
The baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of 330 MPa at 1273 K.
The baseline TiVNbTa alloy reaches 423 MPa compressive strength at 30% strain and 1273 K.
Purified TiVNbTa will have yield strength significantly above 330 MPa at 1273 K.
Purified TiVNbTa will have compressive strength significantly above 423 MPa at 1273 K.
Purified TiVNbTa will preserve the required strain capacity near 30% at 1273 K.
The proposed intervention is effective for service temperatures up to approximately 1273 K.
Long-term structural and mechanical stability of TiVNbTa at potential service temperatures remains uncertain.

contradictions.description: The intervention proposes drastically removing oxygen and nitrogen, while the mechanism claims that the intervention preserves dislocation-pinning benefits from a uniform interstitial distribution. Removing the strengthening interstitials and retaining their strengthening benefit are not reconciled.

The hypothesis attributes preserved solid-solution strengthening to impurity minimization, but the cited mechanism identifies those same interstitial impurities as initial contributors to solid-solution strengthening. An optimal residual concentration or alternative source of strengthening is not specified.
